Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Australian players. There are 25 overs left in the Day as the Windies openers, skipper Kraigg Brathwaite and debutant Tagenarine Chanderpaul walk out to the middle. Mitchell Starc has been handed the new ball and is raring to go. There are three slips and a gully in place. Let's play...

An update on the pitch from Brendon Julian before the West Indian reply. He says that West Indies will opt for the heavy roller which will be used for seven minutes. He adds that the pitch will be nice and hard but there will be something for the Aussie quicks. It will depend on making the Windies batters play at more deliveries.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

West Indies will be mightily relieved that they don't have to toil further in the field but they will be aware of the incoming threat as well. None of the bowlers proved to be effective for them and they were simply inconsistent with their lines and lengths. Skipper Kraigg Brathwaite who is a part-time off-spinner probably troubled the Aussie batters the most and even got a couple of in-form batters out. The Windies openers will have a big role to play when they come out to bat. Will we see the visitors emulating the hosts with the bat? Or will the Aussie pace attack derail the Windies batting line up? Find out as the Windies reply is up next.

Right then, heartbreak right in the end for Travis Head and Pat Cummins has finally decided to declare with the score being 598/4. It has been just a cakewalk for the hosts on Day 2 as more than 300 runs were scored in a little over two sessions and they lost just a couple of wickets as well. It was Marnus Labuschagne who brought up his second double-ton in Test cricket in the first session and then after he got out, the pair of Steven Smith and Travis Head added on 196 runs and the former notched up a classy double-century as well but Head ended up a run short of what would have been a stellar hundred. They will now be hoping that their bowlers continue the good work.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Oh, tragedy here for Travis Head! He is gone on 99 and Australia have declared. A shortish delivery by Kraigg Brathwaite that is pushed quicker as well and around off. Head tries to late-cut it but gets an inside edge that goes onto knock over the stumps. He would be disappointed but it has been a superb knock from the South Australian. Australia declare at 598/4!

Gets to his double-hundred now! What a fantastic flawless knock this has been! Takes off his helmet and soaks in the applause from his teammates and this healthy crowd here at the Optus Stadium. A shortish delivery, around off. Smith chops it to backward point and takes a single that takes him to his fourth double-hundred in Test cricket.
A flatter delivery on middle. Smith works it to mid-wicket and fails to find the gap.
Tossed up, on middle. Head shimmies down the track and knocks it to long on for a single.
Smith calls for the second run straightaway and gets two! Touch shorter and around off. Smith waits for it and just works it towards wide of long on for a couple. Smith moves to 199!
Tossed up, on off. Head drives it to long off for a single.
Fires it full and down the leg side. Head clips it to short fine leg and Smith looks for a single but is sent back.
Fires it quicker and outside off. Smith cuts it to deep point for an easy single again. This is just poor bowling, Windies are making way too easy for these Australian batters.
Short and outside off. Head cuts it to sweeper cover for a single.
Touch shorter and outside off. Smith cuts it to backward point for a single.

It seems like the declaration is coming soon. A few of the Australian players are seen standing by around the boundary ropes and the wait is probably for Smith and Head who are both nearing their milestones.
Angles it on the pads and it is bit quicker. Smith works it to square leg for a single.
On the shorter side, on off. Smith just lifts it over the bowler's head with a straight blade and comes back for the second run.
A fuller delivery, around off. Head drives it to sweeper cover for a single.
On the shorter side and angling into middle. Head goes deep in his crease and knocks it in the gap towards deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Bowls it full and on middle. Smith works it to deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up on middle. Head knocks it down to long on for a single.
Oh, a full toss angling into the body. Head is surprised by this delivery but manages to work it to deep square leg for a single.
Bowls almost a yorker, on off. Head digs it out back to the bowler.
Angles it on the pads again. Smith works it to square leg for a single.
Shorter and down the leg side. Smith tries to clip it away but misses.
Tossed up on off. Head drives it to long on for a single.
FOUR! Poor delivery and punished! This is a full delivery on leg. Head paddles it towards the fine leg fence for another boundary.
Roston Chase (29-2-127-0) to continue operating from the opposite end.
Bowls it fuller and on middle. Head works it to mid-wicket for a single.
Touch shorter on middle. Smith works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A flatter delivery on middle. Smith works it towards the leg side.
Flatter and quicker one on off. Smith tries to punch it but gets beaten.
On the shorter side, on off. Head punches it to long off for a single.
FOUR! Head starts off the session with a boundary! Shorter and angling on the pads. Head tucks it fine and the ball races away towards the fence for a boundary.

We are back for the final session on Day 2! The umpires are out in the middle as Steven Smith and Travis Head can be seen waiting patiently on the sidelines. The West Indies players can be seen in a huddle before taking the field. It will be the skipper Kraigg Brathwaite to continue with his off-breaks after the interval.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

West Indies, on the other hand, are looking a tired outfit now. The batting has been top class and so their bowlers are now looking completely ineffective. There were too many boundary deliveries as well in this session and things are only going to get tougher for West Indies from hereon. Expect Australia to come out all guns blazing in the final session. We shall be back at 12.50 pm IST (7.20 am IST) for what promises to be an exciting final session.

Australian domination continues! A wicketless session with 166 runs in it and they are now closing in on 600. This session had more shades of aggression in it as well and we might see the declaration anytime soon after Tea. Talking about the batters, Smith took his fluency a notch higher in this session and is looking good for a memorable double ton here. It has been an absolutely flawless knock from the maestro so far and Travis Head at the other end did what he always does and would be looking to notch up a quick-fire century here as well. He is making most of this tired looking Windies bowling attack now and it is all about how much more Australia want to score from hereon.
Another low full toss around off, Travis Head hits it through mid on for a run and that will be Tea on Day 2. Australia are 568/3!
A nice and juicy full toss on off stump, trying to induce a big shot from the batter. Steven Smith just knocks it along the ground and to long on for a single.
This is full and angled in at the toes, Travis Head flicks it away through square leg for one more.
This is full and on off stump, driven down to long on for a single.
Nicely drifted from around off stump, Smith leans on and pushes it back to the bowler.
This is drifted down the leg side and Smith leaves it alone for the keeper to collect.
Around the pads, this is nudged away towards mid-wicket for a single.
Slightly flighted around off, Smith pushes it towards silly mid off.
Floated up on the pads, Steven Smith whips it through mid-wicket and races back for the second. Excellent running.
Full and straight, drilled down to long on for a single.

FOUR! A real long hop from Kraigg Brathwaite and it is duly punished. This is slower and served around leg stump. Head pulls it off the back foot and in between the fielders at fine leg and deep square leg for a boundary. Head is now scoring at run-a-ball.
On a good length and angled across the off stump, Steven Smith stays deep and just punches it through mid off for a single.
Gives it a nice loop and bowls it well outside off. Travis Head presses forward but leaves it alone.
Flighted delivery around off, this is just eased through covers for one.
A tad bit short and on middle and leg, Head works it off the back foot towards mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! Poor effort in the deep from Kemar Roach. Chase tosses it up well wide of the off stump. Travis Head has to reach for it but he is able to generate good power on the cut shot. This is hit well in front of the square on the off side and Roach runs around from deep cover but fails to stop it with his boot.
Slows it up a touch and shortens the length as well. Smith waits for it and just drops it onto the leg side for one more.
A full toss now around middle, Head heaves it past the diving man at wide mid on for a single.

FOUR! Edgy boundary but Steven Smith and Australia won't mind it one bit. This is angled across the off stump quicker and on a shorter length as well. Smith looks to punch it off the back foot but gets an outside edge that runs away into the third man fence.
Flatter again and angling into leg stump, Head forces it through mid on for one.
FOUR! Immaculate placement from Travis Head. Quicker and flatter, Head rocks back and punches it in front of covers for a boundary.
Slower and shorter around the leg stump, Steven Smith works it in front of the square on the leg side and looks for two but has to settle for the single.
This is quicker and darted into the leg stump, Travis Head backs away and hits it through mid off for a run.
Kraigg Brathwaite brings himself back on and starts with a flighted delivery around off. Steven Smith wrists it through mid-wicket for a single.

Another good effort in the deep by Tagenarine Chanderpaul. This is full and around off, Steven Smith drives it through extra cover. Chanderpaul runs to his left from long off and dives in to make the stop. Three runs are taken.
Chase spears one into the middle stump but Steven Smith is able to jam it out.
A low full toss now on leg stump, Head knocks it down to long on and turns the strike over.
Shorter and around leg stump, this is turned off the back foot through backward square leg for a run.

Was there an edge on it? No, it is given as byes. This is quicker and flatter, close to the off stump. Travis Head looks to cut it late but gets beaten on the outside edge. The keeper fumbles as well and the batters get a bye.
Short of a length and angling into off stump, this is punched down to long on for one.
FOUR! Nicely done by Travis Head. This is banged in halfway down the track and outside off, Head hops up and just ramps it over short third man for a boundary.
Length again around off, this is eased away through covers for a run.

More signs of aggression from Steven Smith. Good length around off, Smith opens up his arms and looks to smash it over wide mid on but mistimes it. The ball clears mid on but it will only be a couple of runs.
On a length but angling onto the pads, this is worked away behind square on the leg side for a single.
Roach comes from around the wicket and angles in a very full ball on off stump. Head plays it towards mid off.
This is full and well outside off, Smith leans on and drives it through covers for a run.
Tossed up around middle, Travis Head looks for the slog sweep but ends up heaving it through wide mid on for a brace.
On the shorter side and around off, Travis Head rocks back and punches it through extra cover for a couple of runs.
Flighted, well outside off and turning in a bit. Smith waits for it and plays it with an angled bat through the vacant slip cordon for a single.
Pushed through quicker and on a nagging length around off, Steven Smith defends it off the front foot.
Nicely drifted onto middle and leg, Smith drives it straight towards mid on.
Quicker and shorter, close to the off stump, Travis Head chops it in front of covers and picks up a quick run.
Back of a length and around off, Steven Smith stays on the back foot and just dabs it down to backward point.
Cut away and that will be FIFTY for Travis Head and he's got there pretty quickly as well. Short of a length and outside off, Head presses back and cuts it through point for a single.
Good length, around middle and this is just blocked out by Head.

A bit of aggression now from Steven Smith but he mistimes it badly. This is short and outside off, Smith advances and looks to force the big shot square on the off side but gets a top edge over the cover region for a single.
Back to over the wicket now for the right-hander. This is full and trying to shape it in from well outside off, Smith leaves it alone.
Kemar Roach comes back into the attack and starts with a length ball that is angled into the pads from around the wicket. Travis Head works it 'round the corner for a single.
Chase keeps his length a bit short again, turning into middle. Smith works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Nice placement! A shortish delivery and outside off. Smith stays deep in his crease and slaps it through the extra-cover region for a boundary.
Fuller delivery on off. Smith works it to mid-wicket this time.
A flatter delivery on off. Smith blocks it out.
Touch shorter and on middle. Smith works it to deep backward square leg for a couple.

Nice turn and bounce there! Tossed up and outside off. Head goes for a big wild slog-sweep but misses as the ball turns away from him sharply. The keeper fails to collect it cleanly and the batters take three byes as the ball goes towards the third man region.
FOUR! That's a shot of a man in form! Joseph keeps it short again, bit of room this time. Smith waits for it and just guides it over the slip fielders for a boundary.
Good bouncer by Joseph! Angles this short delivery into the body at a good height and Smith also does well to sway away from the line of the ball.
On the shorter side, on off. Head rides the bounce and fends it towards the off side for a single.
Back of a length, on off. Smith dabs it to point for a single.

FOUR! 150 up for Steven Smith! He is back at his best now! He has looked in total control right throughout this knock and is looking good for many more. A fullish delivery on the pads this time. Smith leans forward and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Joseph bowls it on a fullish length, on off at 138.2 kph. Smith drives it off the inside half of his blade towards mid-wicket.
Shortish length and outside off. Smith cuts it to deep backward point for a single.
Floated up on the stumps, Smith just blocks it out.
Slower through the air and bowled around middle, Smith nudges it onto the leg side.
Looped up, full and on off stump, Smith flicks it away but the fielder at short mid-wicket makes a good stop.
Nicely flighted, around off and Steven Smith just eases it towards mid on.

A flatter delivery on off. Smith plays it back to the bowler.
A full delivery on the pads. Head clips it through mid-wicket nicely hut Holder does well to stop it inside the playing area. Three taken.
Good pacy bouncer this! Jospeh fires a bouncer on off. It zips off the surface and Head ducks under it.

A good-length delivery on off. Smith tries to defend it but the ball catches the outside edge of his blade and the ball rolls towards the gully region.
Back of a length and angles it on middle and leg. head works it to fine leg for a single.
On the shorter side, on middle. Smith goes back and punches it to mid on.
Turnning into middle and leg. Bit flatter and Smith works it towards square leg.
Loopy delivery on off. Head drives it firmly to long off for a single.
Bowls another fullish delivery on off. Smith reaches the pitch of the ball and works it to long on for a single.
Pushes quicker and on off. Smith blocks it out solidly.
Tossed up on middle. Head drives it to long on for a single.
Joseph keeps it a touch shorter and outside off. Smith leaves it alone.
On the shorter side, on middle. Smith works it towards deep backward square leg for a couple.
Bowls a full delivery on off. Smith drives it back to the bowler.
On a length and on off. Smith defends it towards the leg side.
On the shorter side and around off. Head rides the bounce and dabs it to backward point for a single.
Back of a length and outside off. Angled across the batter nicely and Head lets it go.

Drinks! It has been a comfortable first hour after the lunch interval for Australia as runs have flown and they are itching towards the 500-run mark. Steven Smith has just got back into his groove and is looking to score a big one here whereas Travis Head has been scoring runs at will. West Indies needed to press the issue after the break but instead the first few overs were just poor, allowing the new batter to get easy runs and all they can do now is keep on probing because it seems to be another long day in the field for them.
Touch shorter and on off. Head goes back and punches it to covers for a single.

NOT OUT! Tossed up on middle from 'round the wicket. Head goes for a big sweep shot but misses. The ball hits his pads and Chase makes a loud appeal. However, the umpire turns it down. It looks close to the naked eye and Kraigg Brathwaite goes for the DRS. The replays roll and the UltraEdge shows no bat there. Then, the Ball Tracking rolls and it shows that the ball is going over the middle pole. So, the original decision will stay and Head will continue.

There is an appeal for an LBW but the umpire turns it down. Kraigg Brathwaite has a long think about it and opts for the review. The UltraEdge is checked first and there is no bat involved. Ball Tracking then shows that the ball is going over the stumps and the original decision stands. West Indies lose a review as well.

Pushes it quicker on off. Head tries to drive it but hits it off the inside half of his blade back to the bowler.

Tossed up, on off. Head drives it to long off for a single.

Back of a length, on off. Smith blocks it onto the tuf.

A length delivery on middle by Holder. Smith works it to mid-wicket for a single.
Holder keeps it on the shorter side, on off. Head rides the bounce and dabs it towards the off side for a single.
Shortish length again and it is outside off. Head tries to cut it again but misses this time.

Holder bowls it short and on off. Smith pulls it through mid-wicket and takes three as the fielder makes a good diving stop near the ropes.
Shorter and on off. Head goes back and punches it back to the bowler.

Pushes it on middle and leg. Head works it towards the leg side.
Flatter and quicker again on middle. Head works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR BYES! Fires it down the leg side. Head tries to clip it but misses. The keeper misses it too and the ball races away towards the fine leg fence.

Around the top of off, this one just skids through and Steven Smith does well to keep it out.

Around middle and leg, kept out by Head.

Back of a length and over middle stump, Steven Smith hops and works it away past square leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length and around off, Smith defends it out with a dead bat.

Welcome back folks! We are all ready for the post-Lunch session as West Indies players make their way out to the middle. Steven Smith also strides out to the middle along with the new batter Travis Head. We can expect Aussies to go a bit hard in this session. Kraigg Brathwaite to resume his over. Here we go...
… DAY 2, SESSION 2 …

West Indies have toiled hard on the field and this is not what they wanted this morning after a challenging Day 1 but they mostly have themselves to blame for this. The Windies just weren't attacking enough when the second new ball was still doing enough and some of the field placements were questionable. A couple of bowlers did bowl well in patches but have found it hard to create wicket-taking opportunities. The skipper Kraigg Brathwaite did get a big breakthrough late in the session which might prove to be a catalyst for them. Will we finally see the visitors pressing the issue in the afternoon session? Or will the Aussies continue to score runs freely? Join us at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) to find out.

The Aussies started the day in a position of promise and they have only gone and cemented their dominance further. Marnus Labuschagne and Steven Smith went on to score a double-century and century respectively as they made the opposition work hard in the field with not just their strokeplay but also with their running. The pair was looking unstoppable and looked all set to bat for another whole session together but in the final over before the interval, the 251-run stand was broken as Labuschagne was dismissed after just reaching a sensational double-ton.

Session summary - 28.1 overs, 109 runs and 1 wicket. So, another session of Test cricket has flown by and Australia are the ones who have just gone from strength to strength and seem to be well on course for a mammoth total. West Indies will feel that they have been static in the way they have approached the morning session but that big wicket on the stroke of lunch will certainly provide them with a lot of inspiration when they take the field again.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Oh, what an anti-climax! Marnus Labuschagne departs just at the stroke of Lunch and that ends a marathon knock from a fantastic cricketer. Kraigg Brathwaite brings himself on and fires a flatter and touch shorter delivery, around off from 'round the wicket. Marnus Labuschagne goes back and tries to steer it square off the wicket on the off side. However, the ball bounces a touch more and takes an outside edge of his blade and Joshua Da Silva behind the stumps takes a sharp catch. Marnus Labuschagne is disappointed and it will be Lunch on Day 2! Marnus Labuschagne gets a standing ovation and Australia are 402 for 3 at Lunch on Day 2!
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Kraigg Brathwaite

Commentary.Commentary: On the shorter side and around off. Marnus Labuschagne punches it through point for a single.

FOUR! Marnus Labuschagne gets to his double century in style! What a player this man is turning out to be! The hunger for runs is just amazing and he just continues to grow in stature. Seales a bowls an overpitched delivery, outside off. Marnus Labuschagne leans forward and drives it crisply through covers for a lovely boundary. Takes off his helmet and soaks in the applause from this healthy crowd here at the Optus stadium.
Seales again bowls it full and on middle. Marnus Labuschagne clips it to mid-wicket.
Seales bowls a fullish delivery and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne resists the temptation to drive and leaves it.
Short and outside off. Smith cuts it to deep point for a single.
Takes a single and moves to 199! A fullish delivery, around off. Marnus Labuschagne drives it left of mid off for a single.
Nicely tossed up delivery on off. Smith gets a good stride forward and defends it.
Fires it flatter and quicker on off. Smith fends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Poor delivery and punished! Short delivery and outside off. Smith rocks back and cuts it through covers for a boundary.
Bit quicker and turning into leg. Smith just works it to the leg side.
Tossed up, on off. Marnus Labuschagne skips down the track and pushes it to long on for a single.
Shortish length and around off. Smith chops it to deep backward point for a single.
Keeps it on the shorter side, on off. Marnus Labuschagne defends it right under his eyes.
Seales again pulls his length back, around off. Smith punches it to deep backward point for a single.
On a length, on off. Smith with a solid block again.
Shortish length again, around off. Smith first sets up to pull it but then checks his shot and just blocks it.
Short and wide outside off. Smith cuts it to deep cover for a couple. Nothing happening for the West Indies bowlers at the moment.
Back of a length, on middle. Smith fends it calmly towards the leg side.
Shortish delivery again and outside off. Smith cuts it to deep point for a single.
On the shorter side, around off. Smith tries to cut it but gets an inside edge that rolls towards the leg side.
Flatter and quicker on middle. Smith blocks it out.
Touch shorter on off. Marnus Labuschagne goes back and punches it to covers for a single.
Fuller and on the leg. Smith clips it to square leg for a single.
Good use of the wrists! Tossed up on middle. Smith reaches the pitch of the ball and works it past the diving fielder at widish mid on and takes two runs.
On the shorter side, on middle. Marnus Labuschagne clips it to mid-wicket.
A length delivery on off. That bounces sharply and hits high on Marnus Labuschagne's blade as he defends it.
Joseph bowls it a tad short, on middle. Marnus Labuschagne defends it from his crease.
Good-length delivery, outside off. Marnus Labuschagne leaves it alone.
Angles a length delivery on the pads. Smith tucks it to fine leg for a single.
Lands a length delivery on middle. Smith works it towards the leg side.
Touch shorter and around off. Marnus Labuschagne punches it through point for a couple.
Turning into leg and fuller in length too. Marnus Labuschagne tries to tuck it towards the leg side. He gets a faint part of his blade and keeper moves to his left but fails to catch it.
A flatter delivery on middle. Marnus Labuschagne blocks it out.

Here it is....29th Test century for Steven Smith! He equals Don Bradman's record of 29 centuries and raises his bat as his wife in the balcony applauds his effort along with his teammates and this crowd at the Optus stadium. This is a fuller delivery on middle. Smith drives it to long on for a single.
A solid block! Tossed up on middle. Smith blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up, on middle. Smith works it to square leg.
On a good length and around off. The ball nips back in and Marnus Labuschagne leaves it as the ball goes very close past the off stump.
Lovely delivery! Lands on a good length and outside off. The ball straightens a bit after pitching and beats the putside edge of Marnus Labuschagne's blade as he tries to defend it.
Alzarri Joseph goes wide of the crease and angles it on middle and leg. A length delivery and Smith works it past square leg for a single.
Angles a length delivery on middle. Smith with a solid block. The wait continues as the crowd gets excited.
On a length and around off. Smith guides it towards the gully fielder.
NO BALL!  Abit fullish delivery, outside off. Smith resists the temptation to drive it and lets it go. A  No Ball is called for overstepping.
On a good length and outside off. Smith lets it go with ease.
Tossed up on middle. Smith drives it off the inside half of his blade to long on for a single. Smith will retain the strike!
Turning into middle and leg. Smith works it towards the leg side.
FOUR! Smith moves to 97 now! Chase bowls it on middle. Smith reaches the pitch of the ball and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On the shorter side again, around off. Marnus Labuschagne punches it through covers for a single.
Shortish length and around off. Smith punches it through backward point for a single.
Chase bowls it full and on the pads. Smith works it to mid-wicket.
Good length and at the stumps, Smith pushes it towards wide mid on for yet another comfortable single.
Hits the length hard does Joseph and bowls it around the hips. Labuschagne just drops it towards mid-wicket and picks up a run.
Good length around the top of off and at almost 141 clicks. Labuschagne gets right behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Good length around off, Labuschagne watches it closely and leaves it alone.
Short again, over middle and Smith pulls it through wide mid on for a single.
This is banged in short over middle and leg and at a good height as well. Marnus Labuschagne goes after it and mistimes the hook shot towards deep square leg for one.

Aerial but lands well short! Roston Chase gives it a nice loop and bowls it around middle. Marnus Labuschagne dances down the track and gets beaten in the flight and ends up dragging the big shot towards deep square leg. Tagenarine Chanderpaul is over there but the ball lands short of him and they get a single.
Slows it up a touch and bowls it on middle, Labuschagne just blocks it out.
On a length and on off stump, Labuschagne backs away and plays it straight towards the cover region.
Tossed up full and outside off, Steven Smith drives it through covers towards the sweeper and picks up a single.
Flighted, around middle and Steven Smith just defends it out.
This is floated up on the pads, Smith nudges it towards mid-wicket.
Nice shape on that one. This is very full and on off stump, shaping away as well, Labuschagne manages to keep it out.
Joseph bowls it full and closer to the off pole at 137.4 clicks but Labuschagne makes an assured leave.
Length ball around off, Labuschagne defends it out.

FOUR! Short and wide, Marnus Labuschagne throws his hands at it and gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies away just out of reach of the jumping man at gully and into the third man fence. Alzarri Joseph doesn't seem impressed with that effort.
Fullish delivery outside off and shaping away, Labuschagne watches it go past him and through to the keeper.
Back of a length and around off, this is dabbed down towards backward point.
Nicely tossed up, on middle and leg, Smith presents the full face of the bat and pushes it towards mid on.
Flighted delivery, Steven Smith works it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter one around middle and this one keeps low. Labuschagne backs away and forces it down to long off for a single.
Tossed up around middle, Labuschagne advances but then has to adjust and keep it out.
Floated up and turning down leg, Smith just nudges it behind square on the leg side and rotates the strike.
Chase starts off with a quicker one on middle and leg, Labuschagne backs away and pushes it towards cover for a quick single.
Time for some spin now. Roston Chase (15-2-63-0) is into the attack.
Good length over middle stump and blocked out towards short mid-wicket.
Keeps it on a fuller length but pushes it wide of the off stump, Smith shoulders arms at it.
Fullish length around off, Steven Smith leaves it alone.
Good fielding. Full again and on the pads, flicked away to the right of the man at mid-wicket who makes a good stop. They do take the single though.
Full and straight, this is punched firmly back past the fielder but straight to the man at mid off.
Pitches it up now around middle, Labuschagne defends it from inside his crease.

Full and on the pads, Steven Smith uses his wrists and whips it through the vacant spaces around mid-wicket and picks up three more runs. A no ball is also called as Kemar Roach has overstepped. The 200-run stand between these two is up and neither batter is showing any signs of slowing down.

Drinks! Australian batters are taking this game away from the Windies now. They have looked very comfortable and have scored at a good rate too. Windies, on the other hand, are looking pretty flat. They could not bowl consistent lines and lengths and now are starring down the barrel. They need a moment of brilliance from somewhere to lift their spirits up and another poor hour of play will make things quite difficult for them. Can they fightback in the second half of this first session? Let's find out.
Goes a bit fuller and just tightens the line around off stump, Labuschagne doesn't play at it.
On the shorter side yet again and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne opens the face of the bat and guides it to the left of the man at third man for a couple of runs.
Good length on off stump, Smith shuffles across and works it away through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Nicely done! Short and a bit wide again from Joseph. Steven Smith rocks back and just dabs it past the slip cordon and into the third man fence for a boundary.
Pitches it up now in that channel around off and Steven Smith lets it through to the keeper.
Alzarri Joseph starts a new spell with a bit of a loosener. This is short and wide, cut away to deep point for a single by Labuschagne.
Alzarri Joseph is ready to start his first over of the day. He bowled 15 overs on Day 1 but could not find a breakthrough.
Good length around off, just seaming away a touch but Smith is able to defend it out.
Lovely bowling! Roach goes a bit fuller and angles it in from around off. The ball straightens after pitching and zips past the outside edge of Smith's willow.
Back of a length and close to the off pole. Labuschagne looks to punch off the back foot but gets an inside edge that goes past the stumps and towards short fine leg. They pick up a single.
This is angled into middle and leg, Labuschagne just nudges it towards short mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, Labuschagne looks to play away from the body but the ball keeps a bit low and beats the outside edge.
Full and straight, Smith flicks it down to fine leg and turns the strike over.
Length ball around off, Steven Smith shuffles across the off stump and works it away through mid-wicket for a single.
A touch fuller and angling into the pads, Smith keeps it out on the leg side.
Banged in short and over the stumps, Smith just ducks under it.
Around the top of off, Smith blocks it out.

They run four and not for the first time it has happened in this innings either. Fuller and around off, Smith opens the face of the bat and drives it square through the point region. Jayden Seales chases it down and the ball just slows down before Seales picks it up but it will be four runs.
Good length, on the fifth stump line. The ball just straightens a bit and Steven Smith edges it down with soft hands towards second slip.
Fullish length around the pads, this is flicked away 'round the corner for a single.
This is full and outside off, trying to induce the drive but Smith leaves it alone.
Length ball, angling it in from around the top of off stump, Smith solidly keeps it out.
Just a fraction shorter and around off, this one nips back in a touch as well. Labuschagne taps it towards cover-point for one more.
Goes full and keeps the line around off. Labuschagne defends it under his eye line.
Drop and run! Good length around off stump, Steven Smith just dabs it down towards silly point and races through for the single.
Kemar Roach (21-3-69-0) is back into the attack now.
Length ball angling into middle ane leg, this is worked away onto the leg side.
Fuller in length around off and swinging back into the batter. Labuschagne just pushes it towards mid on.

A strong shout of 'no' from Steven Smith. Fullish delivery, around off stump and almost reversing into the batter. Labuschagne gets an inside edge towards square leg and looks for one but is sent back.
Another easy single. Good length, around off, eased away towards the vacant backward point region for a run.
WIDE! This is banged in halfway down the track and over leg stump. The ball goes well over the batter's head and a wide is called.
Good length, trying to angle it in from outside off. Steven Smith puts a big stride forward and looks to defend but gets hit on the pads.
On a hard length and outside off, Labuschagne just nudges it down with soft hands behind point and picks up a single.
Holder angles a length delivery on off. Smith is as calm as ever and defends it right of the bowler.
On a length and around leg. Smith tries to leave it and gets hit high on the pads.
Shortish delivery and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne cuts it to deep point for a single.

That's an easy single, you don't want to give these singles away easily. On a length, on middle. Smith works it behind square on the leg side and takes a single as the fielder there is bit slow to approach that ball.
Bangs it short and around leg. Smith leaves it alone.

In the air...but safe! Holder bangs it short on off. Marnus Labuschagne tries to pull it off the front foot. He, however, gets a top edge this time that goes aerially but falls well short of the deep square leg fielder. Single taken.
Lands it on a length and outside off. Smith watches it till the end and lets it go.
Back of a length and angling into leg. Smith tries to flick it but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
On the shorter side, around off. Marnus Labuschagne dabs it towards the off side for a single.
Mayers hits that good length again, on off. Marnus Labuschagne blocks it solidly from his crease.
Lands it on a length again and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne stays patient and lets it go.
Good-length delivery, around off. Marnus Labuschagne leaves it.
Bangs it short and angles it into middle and leg. Smith ducks under it.
Shortish delivery on off. Marnus Labuschagne pulls it to square leg. Bonner half-stops it and a single is taken.
Goes fuller and on middle. Smith flicks it well in front of square and takes three runs. Good running again.
On a length, on middle. Marnus Labuschagne clips it behind square on the leg side for a single.

FOUR! In the gap and Marnus Labuschagne gets another boundary! A shortsih delivery that nips back on on off. It cramps Marnus Labuschagne for room and he just tries to guide it towards the off side. Gets a bit of outside edge that goes in the gap wide of the diving first slip fielder for a boundary.
On a good length and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne leaves it alone.
Good shape into the batter. A fullish delivery swinging into off. Smith fends it towards the leg side.
On a good length again and this time a bit closer to the off stump. Smith goes forward to defend it but the ball seams away a touch and beats the outside edge of his blade.
Good-length delivery, outside off. Smith lets it go.
On the shorter side and on off. Marnus Labuschagne pulls it off the inside half of his blade to deep backward square leg for a single.
On a length and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne lets it go.

FOUR! Oh, just past the stumps! Shortish delivery and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne tries to pull it. However, the ball goes off the inside edge and just past the stumps towards the fine leg fence for a boundary.
WIDE! Bowls a fullish and widish delivery way outside off. Marnus Labuschagne leaves it.
Kyle Mayers (11-2-24-1) is into the attack now.

Back of a length, on off at 124.5 kph. Smith blocks it onto the turf. Aussie batters have looked pretty comfortable so far as West Indies have neither got their lines and lengths right nor any great movement off the turf or in air.
Angles a length delivery on middle. Marnus Labuschagne clips it to deep square leg for an easy single.
Shortish and wider outside off. Easy leave for Marnus Labuschagne this time.
Lands a good length delivery again, around off. Marnus Labuschagne lets it go again.
On a length and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne makes an easy leave this time.
On a good length and around off. Marnus Labuschagne tries to block it off his front foot. However, the ball straightens a bit after pitching and beats the outside edge of his blade.
Beautiful delivery! Lands this in that corridor of uncertainity and Smith gets beaten as he tries to defend it.
Overpitched delivery on off. Smith times his straight drive quite well. However, Roach is alert and stops it with his right hand.
Serves a fullish delivery on off. Smith with a solid block here.
Angling into middle on off. Roach went wider of the crease there and Smith defends it to mid on.
Yet again after bowling a good delivery, he drifts on the pads. A fullish delivery and Marnus Labuschagne easily flicks it to deep square leg for a single.
Serves it on a good length, on off. Marnus Labuschagne defends it from his crease. Roach needs to be consistent with this line and length.
Holder bangs it short again on middle. Marnus Labuschagne pulls it quite well this time and takes three as the ball goes towards the deep square leg region before the fielder cuts it off.
That's a good one! Bowls a bouncer, around leg. Good bounce and zip on this delivery as Marnus Labuschagne fails to get any bat on his hook shot.
Touch shorter and outside off. Smith rides the bounce and punches it to deep point where Tagenarine Chanderpaul does well to keep it to just a single.
A fullish delivery on middle. Marnus Labuschagne pushes it. However, he gets the inside half of his blade to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length and outside off. Marnus Labuschagne leaves it.
Holder with a good-length delivery, on off. Marnus Labuschagne blocks it off the front foot.
Serves it on a length, on off at 126 clicks and Smith defends it nicely showing a full face of his blade.
Roach bangs it short and not much pace on this delivery. On off and Marnus Labuschagne pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length, on off. Good bounce for Roach as the ball hits the higher part of Smith's blade as he tries to defend it. The ball rolls towards the off side and a single is taken.
Touch on the shorter side, around off. Marnus Labuschagne dabs it to backward point for an easy single. The partnership between these two besties is now 150!
A fullish delivery on off. Marnus Labuschagne drives it back to the bowler.

Now he finds that channel! Lands it on a good length, around off, angles it into the batter. Marnus Labuschagne is neither back or forward and ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to defend it.
Back of a length and outside off. Smith resists the temptation to go at a widish delivery and lets it go. So, just one run from Holder's first over of the day.
Touch short of good length and on off. Smith defends it right under his eyes.
Lands it on a good length at a gentle pace again. Smith makes an easy leave. Not much swing so far for the Windies.
On a length, on off. Smith with a solid block now.
He drifts it way down the leg side this time. Smith first sets up to flick it but then decides to let it go.
Holder starts off with a fullish delivery on off at 124 kph. Marnus Labuschagne defends it with soft hands towards the off side and takes his first run of the day. 300 up for Australia!
Jason Holder (16-6-29-0) to operate from the other end.

Finally bowls it fuller but ends up drifting on the pads. Smith is ready for it as he flicks it through mid-wicket and the batters run four. Very good running and this is a nice positive start from the Aussies.
Roach has not found his length so far. He bowls it on a shortish length again and outside off. Smith lets it go again.
Gets his length bit fuller this time. On a good length and outside off. Smith decides to leave it alone.
Tad shorter again by Roach angling into middle. Smith works it towards the leg side.
Shorter in length again and outside off. Smith tries to punch it this time but gets an inside edge that goes just past the stumps.
Roach starts off with a short and wide delivery outside off. Smith cuts it through covers for a couple. Good positive start for Smith.

We are all ready for the second day of this Test match! The Windies players have made their way into the middle. Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne, the two overnight Australian batters have also made their way out to the middle now. Kemar Roach to start with the ball. Here we go...

Australia have laid down the marker for the rest of the game with their batters bossing Day 1. After David Warner fell early, Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne put on a big stand that put the hosts on top of the proceedings. Usman Khawaja fell but Marnus Labuschagne went on to build another century stand with Steven Smith and brought an individual ton as well. Aussies will look for more of the same on Day 2. Stay tuned as the morning session isn't far away.

West Indies started with a lot of promise in the field as youngster Jayden Seales got rid of David Warner early in the day but after that, they found it tough going for a long time. Kyle Mayers' underrated skills as a bowler came to the rescue of the visitors as he broke a crucial stand but yet again the Windies couldn't capitalise. They would be hoping that the pitch quickens up and they can get early wickets on Day 2 to get back in the contest.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 2 of the first Test match between Australia and West Indies from the Optus Stadium in Perth. Day 1 saw the hosts put on a stellar show with the bat Marnus Labuschagne notching up a brilliant ton. Will we see another run fest on Day 2 as well?
… DAY 2, SESSION 1 …

Right then, that is all we have from his absorbing opening day of the first Test match. West Indies need to do some heavy lifting on Day 2 now to make their way back into this game. Will the Windies fightback? Or will Australia consolidate their position? We shall get all our answers when the play resumes on Thursday, 1st of December at 7.50 am IST (2.20 am GMT). Our build-up though as you know, begins a lot earlier. Do join us for the same. Cheers!

The day started with Jayden Seales getting rid of David Warner early. However, Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne then showed some great grit and determination to ride through a tough period when West Indies were really bowling well in the first session. Runs started flowing bit quickly in the afternoon session for the Aussies as Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne both got to their fifties. Mayers then brought some life back into the Windies camp with a wicket late in the second session. However, after that Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne did not given an inch to the West Indies and now the home team is looking all set to dominate this Test match. The first session will be crucial on Day 2 and West Indies need to come up with better plans and execution going ahead in this Test match.

Marnus Labuschagne is down for a chat. He says that whenever you finish a day with almost 300 runs and just 2 wickets lost it is a great day and they will now look to get a big total on board. Adds that it helps coming from Brisbane to play on bouncy wickets like this one and if you're patient and the technique is sound, you can score runs here. Mentions that whenever you aren't scoring runs there's a bit of doubt but it is all about trusting the process. Ends by saying that his wife and daughter made the trip to watch him play here and that makes this hundred a bit more special.

West Indies, well, they tried hard but the Australian batters were too good on the day. Kraigg Brathwaite tried all his options but nothing worked and though there were few plays and misses in between, it was a frustrating day from the Windies' point of view. The second new ball now is eight overs old and West Indies need to make the most of it early on Day 2 if they want to make their way back into this game.

Steven Smith started the final session with a bang stroking a boundary off the first delivery and he just continued the same momentum throughout the session on his way to a fluent 59*. Marnus Labuschagne at the other end was also more proactive in this session and notched up a gritty century and ended with an unbeaten knock of 154 as runs started flowing quickly for the Aussies. They are in a pole position now and we can expect Australian batters to come up with more aggressive intent on Day 2 and they would surely be trying to get their first innings total somewhere over 500 now.

Australia have dominated this session and are in the driver’s seat now at the end of Day 1. A wicketless session with 131 runs added and West Indies after starting this morning on a positive note have not been able to get enough breakthroughs throughout the day to put more pressure on the Aussies.

An inside edge to end Day 1! This is full and angled into leg stump, Steven Smith shuffle across a bit and gets an inside edge down to fine leg for a single. The umpires call for Stumps as Australia finish the Day with 293/2!
Good length around off, Steven Smith leaves it alone.
Angles this one into the stumps, Steven Smith blocks it out.
Good length outside off, this is guided away through backward point for a single.
Pitches it up now on off stump and this is solidly blocked off by Labuschagne.

JAFFA! No idea what happened there! Jason Holder starts off with a good-length delivery that is angled into off stump. Labuschagne looks to block but the ball just seams away off the deck and goes past the shoulder of the blade. Labuschagne smiles as he knows the delivery was too good but Jason Holder is left frustrated.
Jason Holder to bowl the last over of the day!
Around the top of off, this is defended off the back foot.
Mayers goes wider of the crease and angles it in a long way from well outside off. Steven Smith stays back and keeps it out.
Fuller in length but well outside off, easy leave for Smith.
Good length angling down leg. Steven Smith shuffles across and shoulders arms at it.
This is very full again but a lot wider, Labuschagne plays it late and with an angled bat past point for a single.
Kyle Mayers comes back into the attack and serves a yorker-length delivery around middle. Labuschagne jams it out towards short mid-wicket.
A bit fuller and tighter around the off stump. Steven Smith watches it all the way through and leaves it alone.
Good length again but a bit wider and Labuschagne taps it through cover-point to pick up a single.
On a good length and around off, Labuschagne leaves it alone.

150 up for Marnus Labuschagne and it is the fourth time he has surpassed this score in Test matches. This is pitched up outside off, Labuschagne with another cover drive and he gets back for two with ease. This has been a sublime knock so far from him.

FOUR! A valiant effort in the deep but it goes in vain. This is on a good length but well outside off. Labuschagne uses the width on offer and slaps it away behind point. Tagenarine Chanderpaul runs to his left from deep point and puts in the dive but is unable to prevent the boundary. Labuschagne moves on to 149 now.
Full and around off stump, Marnus Labuschagne crouches a bit and caresses it through the cover region for a couple of runs. Good running on that occasion.
Around the top of off, Smith defends this one onto the off side.

Kemar Roach serves this on a good length and angles it in from the off stump. Steven Smith looks to press forward and block but misses and gets hit high on the pads. There is an hopeful appeal for lbw but it has been turned down. There hasn't been a single review throughout the day but desperate times call for desperate as Kraigg Brathwaite does go for it. UltraEdge shows that there is no bat involved and Ball Tracking confirms that the ball is comfortably going over the leg stump.
Just a fraction shorter and wide outside off, Labuschagne presses back and taps it through cover-point for a run.
Pitched up around the fifth stump and shaping away, left alone by Labuschagne.
Full and outside off, Smith opens the face of the blade and drives it square of the wicket for a single.
Length ball, well wide of the off stump, Steven Smith lets it through to the keeper.
Pitches it up on the pads, Labuschagne defends it out. Maiden!
Keeps it full and bowls it in the channel around off. There's just a hint of away shape on it but it is an easy enough leave for Labuschagne to make.
A tad fuller and pulled wider of the off pole. Labuschagne looks to play at it but decides to leave it in the end.
Pitches it up now around off stump, Labuschagne defends it under his eye line.
Full and trying to attack the pads but it is spilled well down the leg side.
On a fullish length and outside off, Labuschagne makes an easy leave.

BEATEN! Kemar Roach with a beautiful comeback delivery that leaves Steven Smith bamboozled. This is served on a good length and angling in from around off. The ball straightens after pitching and Smith just spars at it. The ball zips past the outside edge into the keeper's gloves.
FOUR! Short ball but just not short enough to trouble the batter. This is outside off and Steven Smith fetches it before muscling it away into the mid-wicket fence.
Pitched a bit further up and around middle and leg, Smith punches it towards mid on.
Short and wide, slapped away towards deep cover for a single.
Good length, around off and this one nips back in sharply. Labuschagne looks to block but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

FOUR! Edged away! Fullish length around the off stump, Marnus Labuschagne just gets squares up a touch but plays at it with soft hands. The ball goes off the outside edge and runs through the slip cordon for a boundary.
Good length outside off, Steven Smith leaves it alone.

DROPPED! Tagenarine Chanderpaul almost pulls off a brilliant take in the deep on debut. Fraction shorter and well outside off. Marnus Labuschagne sees the width on offer and throws his hands at it. The ball is slashed away towards deep backward point and the man in the deep seems to pick it up a bit late. Chanderpaul does dive in but the ball falls short. A single is also taken.
On a hard length and well outside off, Steven Smith shoulders arms.
Seales looks to go full and wide but just pushes it beyond the tramline outside off. The umpire lets him off the hook though.
Much better now, pitched up around middle and Labuschagne blocks it off the front foot.
Starts off with a gentle-paced delivery, full and well outside off. Labuschagne leaves it alone for the keeper to collect.
Jayden Seales (11-2-53-1) is ready to partner Kemar Roach with the new ball now.
Pitches it up now around off, Steven Smith drives it firmly towards mid off.
Back of a length and outside off, Labuschagne leans back and taps it through covers for a single.
Roach goes very full and looks to attack the pads. Labuschagne looks to flick it away but gets a leading edge onto the off side.
On a length and pushed wider of the off stump, no shot offered by Labuschagne.
Fullish length around off, Labuschagne defends it out.

Kemar Roach almost produces a wicket straight after taking the new ball. This is full and wide, zipping through. Labuschagne reaches out to drive but the ball beats the bat and there is an appeal for caught behind but the bat clearly hit the ground there.
West Indies have taken the second new ball now! A crucial phase of the game coming up as Kemar Roach (15-3-47-0) is back into the attack.
Tosses it up on middle, Steven Smith looks to drive it straight but hits it towards mid on and is a bit annoyed with himself.
Around the off stump, kept out by Steven Smith.
Loopy delivery around off stump, this is eased down to long on for a single.
Tossed up full and on middle, Labuschagne defends it out.
Flights it up now around off, Labuschagne punches it out towards cover.
On middle and leg, flicked away onto the on side.
On the shorter side and flatter, on off. Marnus Labuschagne goes back and punches it to long off for a single.
A touch shorter and around leg stump, this is played off the back foot towards square leg for a run.
Full and at the stumps, blocked out by Smith.
On the pads again and this is just worked away towards backward square leg.
Around the pads, this is nudged away onto the leg side.

Almost picks up a wicket first ball. Kraigg Brathwaite comes from around the wicket and starts with a round-arm delivery angling across off. Marnus Labuschagne ends up chopping it over first slip for a single.

Fires it on middle and bit fuller too. Smith works it to mid-wicket. Good tight over from Chase this!
Tosses this one up and around off. Smith defends it off the front foot quite nicely again.
Chase bowls it fuller on off. Smith with a solid front foot defence.
Chase with a fullish delivery, around off. Smith seems to be just happy to defend at the moment.
Bowls it quicker and flatter on off. Smith with a solid block again.
Chase bowls it a touch shorter and Smith easily defends it off the back foot.

Joseph tries a short delivery again, on middle. Marnus Labuschagne pulls it well but the fielder at mid-wicket stops it.
Touch shorter and around off. Smith punches it to covers for a single.

Joseph bangs it short and angles it on middle. Marnus Labuschagne tries to pull it but is hurried by this short delivery and gets a top edge. The ball, however, falls in the vacant mid-wicket region and a single is taken.

Touch shorter and on off. Marnus Labuschagne punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Tossed up, on middle from 'round the wicket. Marnus Labuschagne drives it to mid on.
Touch shorter and quicker on middle. It allows Smith to go deep in his crease as he works it to square leg for a single.

On a length, on off. Smith stays in his crease and calmly defends this one.
Bowls a fullish delivery that shapes back a bit into Smith. On middle and Smith defends it towards right of the bowler.
Angles a length delivery on middle. Marnus Labuschagne clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
Joseph lands it on a length, on off. Marnus Labuschagne with a solid block this time.

Finds the edge but it is well short of the slip fielder! On a good length and around off. Marnus Labuschagne presses forward to defend it. He, however, gets a thick outside edge that falls well short of the widish first slip fielder.
Back of a length and around off. Marnus Labuschagne rides the bounce and punches it through backward point for a couple.
Touch shorter and turning into middle and leg. Marnus Labuschagne goes deep in his crease and works it to square leg for a single.

Touch shorter and quicker on off. Marnus Labuschagne punches it to covers. There is good healthy banter going on between Marnus Labuschagne and Joshua Da Silva.

Both the batters are looking very comfortable in the middle and Windies after starting so well in this Test match are looking flat in this session. They need a moment of inspiration from somewhere here otherwise Australia can take this game away from them very quickly. The new ball will be due after 7 overs and that would probably be the last chance for Windies to make an impact. However, if they can get rid of one of these two before the new ball, then they can put more pressure on the Aussies with that new ball. A fascinating final passage of the day coming up...

… DAY 1, SESSION 3 …

West Indies will be a bit disappointed with the fact that they could only pick up the solo wicket in this session. This is mainly due to the lack of energy they brought onto the field right after the Lunch break and conceded runs at an alarming rate. The spin of Roston Chase proved ineffective until the second half of the session but he couldn't trouble the batters much. An inspired change then to bring back Kyle Mayers into the attack worked like a charm as he dismissed Usman Khawaja. But that was it and they failed to pick up another wicket before the interval. The visitors need wickets in the final session to end Day 1 on a high. Will they be able to trouble the Australian middle-order? Find out as the final session isn't far away.

Marnus Labuschagne and Usman Khawaja carried on the good work and improved upon the foundation laid in the opening session. The two batters were able to pick up boundaries at regular intervals and rotate strike in the first hour of the second session. Both got to their fifties and looked good but there came a time when Marnus Labuschagne was troubled a bit and the Khawaja was sent packing. The 142-run stand between those two has put Australia in command here and they will look to score more runs in the final session.

Session Summary - 28 overs, 90 runs and 1 wicket. Yet another riveting session of Test cricket has flown by and at this point Australia would be the happier of the two sides but West Indies do have a bit of momentum going into the Tea interval.

Mayers gets good shape away from the batter and the ball catches the outside edge of Usman Khawaja's blade as he tries to defend it. Joshua Da Silva takes an easy regulation catch and that is exactly what Windies needed to lift their spirits up.
